title: Federal government waives $4.5B of debt on COVID-19 benefits sent to ineligible recipients
summary: The federal government is writing off billions of dollars' worth of outstanding debt related to COVID-19 benefits sent to individuals it later deemed ineligible.

image.caption: The office of Auditor General Karen Hogan, left, released a report this month saying that billions in debt related to COVID-19 benefits sent to ineligible recipients has been written off. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: The federal government is writing off billions of dollars' worth of outstanding debt related to COVID-19 benefits sent to individuals it later deemed ineligible.
Billions in overpaid pandemic-related benefits deemed uncollectable

Last week, the Office of the Auditor General of Canada highlighted that Ottawa had written off approximately $4.5 billion in owed COVID-19 benefits as "uncollectable" during the 2025-26 fiscal year, which ended March 31.
The report noted that's a "significant increase" from $26 million in writeoffs in the previous fiscal year.
Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) told CBC News in a statement that the majority of its pandemic benefit-related writeoffs "pertained to deceased or vulnerable populations."
According to the government's 2026 public accounts report and figures ESDC provided to CBC News, the vast majority of pandemic benefit-related writeoffs took place in the last fiscal year.
Over $5B owed on the books as of July
The Canada Revenue Agency estimates it distributed a total of $14 billion in COVID-19 benefits to individuals it says weren't eligible because they didn't meet the income requirements.
By November 2025, that figure had fallen to about $10 billion, and nearly halved to about $5.56 billion by the end of July.
The agency said in September that the latest debt reduction was due to factors including changes in eligibility and writeoffs.

In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, Ottawa rapidly implemented the Canada emergency response benefit (CERB) under an entirely new piece of legislation. The program remained in place between March and October 2020.

To be eligible for CERB, applicants had to have earned $5,000 in income in the previous 12 months, lost income because of the pandemic and not been receiving employment insurance. The benefit gave recipients $2,000 every four weeks.

items: COVID-19 benefit repayment is hurting low-income Canadians, report says

blocks.text: The CRA has been clear that the Crown retains the right to recover the money it's owed and says it could take legal action against an individual if they have the ability to pay off their debt in full, but allow it to remain unpaid.
David Cummings is a reporter for CBC News.
